commits.message:
fix: labledbox no longer wraps its content twice when rebuilt

labledbox.onBuilding moves the node's children into a label box and a
content box. A second build of the same source node (an ancestor's
unfreeze, a rebuild) ran it again on the already restructured node and
nested a new label/content pair inside the old content.

groupletGrid hit it with additem='phantom' in a form: the phantom card
is mounted before the record loads, then _fullSync renders the loaded
rows under bodyNode.freeze()/unfreeze(), and the unfreeze rebuilds the
phantom too. Every lbl'd field of the phantom showed its label twice.

The 08_phantom_row demo gets a case with phantom cards in a loaded form.

Fixes #1763

feat(grouplet): fillRow and wide cards in a responsive groupletGrid

fillRow lets the cards share the whole row, up to cols of them, so a lone card
takes it all instead of a cols-th; a grouplet declaring card=dict(wide=True)
spans the row.

feat(test): a walk-through of inline docs and grouplets, and a guide to the docs

webpages/gnrwdg/demo_inline_docs.py follows one customer: the record form made
of groupletCards, the shipping addresses as a groupletGrid of the same
resource, the fields of adm.user and a table handler view, each with its ⓘ,
and documentation mode to write the notes in place.

webpages/gnrwdg/test_page_doc.py is a page in the public frame whose own doc,
docs/manual/inline_docs.md, explains how the documentation works: addresses,
manual and notes, documenters, the editor, the inlinedoc storage, the code.
Each block of the page opens its chapter.

feat(doc): the help of fields, cards and blocks in a popup; a page's own doc has a folder

The ⓘ of a field label, of a grouplet card and of a roundedGroup with a
helpcode opens genro.dlg.helpTooltip, a popup at the icon with what the help
panel shows (manual section, link, note, Edit/Add a note). The ⓘ of a page and
of a table keeps the help panel. docHelpButton takes tooltip=True.

doc_folder accepted page:<pkg>/<page>:<helpcode> only, so the "?" of a page
with no maintable (page:<pkg>/<page>:) got a 404 from sys/ep_doc and could not
be documented. It now lives in <pkg>/_pages/<page>/_page.

fix(grouplet): dash select and spinner fields in phantom and entry rows

The phantom row rule dashed only TextBox and TextArea fields, so
FilteringSelect, dbSelect and ComboBox (.dijitComboBox) and spinners
(.dijitSpinner) kept the solid border of the formlet field rule. The
entry card rule missed .dijitSpinner. Both now cover the same widget
classes as the formlet field rule.

feat(doc): the "?" opens the published manual's section in a help panel

The user manual is a Sphinx + myst-parser site (as the applications'
manuals are). A section documents a UI element when the label made from the
element's doc address sits above it:

    field:invc.invoice:customer_id  ->  (help-field-invc-invoice-customer_id)=

A variant suffix lets the profile manuals of one site document the same
element (help-...--operatore). Sphinx writes the labels to objects.inv, the
map read by gnr.web.gnrmanual; the section is cut from the published page
(links and images absolute, no scripts).

- The manuals a user reaches are the adm.helpdoc pages of the group the user
  logged in with, then those linked to no group; the user's own pages decide
  between variants, then the label without variant. A page is an http(s)
  url, a file, or a path of a local storage of the site (read as a file,
  linked at its storage url) for a manual the instance serves itself.
- sys/ep_doc: the page index also lists the addresses with a manual section,
  the fragment carries the section next to the customer's note.
- genro.dlg.helpPanel replaces the doc popup: a panel on the right of the
  page with the section, "Open in the manual", then the customer's note and
  Edit / Add a note for a documenter; Esc or the close button closes it. The
  icon shows when the manual or a note documents the address.
- Hosts: docHelpButton (GnrDomSrc); the page top bar (pageHelp: its table's
  doc for a page of a table, its own otherwise), roundedGroup /
  roundedGroupFrame with helpcode, the toolbar of a table handler view that
  is not the page's (vhelp) and of a form of another table (form_help);
  fields and grouplet cards already had it.
- Demo: test/gnrwdg/test_manual_help with a small manual in test/docs/manual.

feat(doc): docs as Markdown in a documentation storage, edited in place by documenters

Documentation lives as MyST Markdown files with a YAML front matter in the
`documentation` storage service (a local folder of the site when it is not
configured, an S3 bucket in production), one folder per context-sensitive help
address and one file per language, images beside it. The code holds only the
address, derived by convention:
- field:<pkg.table>:<column> for every field() of a table;
- grouplet:<pkg.table|pkg>:<resource> for a card or grid row of a resource;
- page:<pkg>/<page>:<helpcode> for a widget with helpcode outside a table;
- table:<pkg.table>: and package:<pkg>: for the reference.

gnr.web.gnrdocumentation holds the addresses, the front matter, the rendering
(markdown-it-py, CommonMark + tables, raw HTML escaped) and the store: one
listing per table for the index of a page, a save refused when the doc
changed since it was read (409, overwrite on request), images as data urls.
sys/ep_doc serves it to a registered calling page of a logged user; writing
needs the documenter tags `_DOC_,doc_<pkg>`.

Client (genro.dlg): a page sends the addresses of its icons in one request;
an icon shows when its doc exists, and red where it is empty to a documenter
in documentation mode (gnr.docModeVisible, menu line for `_DOC_`). The ⓘ
opens one popup per page (a toggletip) with Edit for a documenter; the editor
is MDEditor in a dialog, images pasted in it are stored next to the doc.

Retired: helper.xml (saveHelperValue, getHelperData, setHelperData, the
developer prompt editor, sys/helpeditor) and the inline / file: HTML doc of
grouplet cards; a card's `doc` is now its address (False opts out).

Also:
- EndpointPermission (gnrcomponents/externalcall) shared with ep_table, whose
  tag check called application.getResourcePermission, which does not exist;
- StorageNode.file_mtimes: one paginated listing on aws_s3, os.walk locally;
- funcApply calls an action that is not written as function(...) (an arrow
  function) instead of failing on its signature;
- the ToastUI editor is pinned (3.2.2) instead of loaded as `latest`;
- the field help icon and the card doc icon are the light Material info icon;
- markdown-it-py is a dependency.

fix(grouplet_grid): copied rows keep every row of their nested grids

A field in a row of a nested groupletGrid was named by its label, which
repeats on every nested row: copying a card with several details wrote
the popup fields of each detail under the same header, and the paste put
them all on the first detail. Its path also carried the nested row key,
and the columns came from one card only, so details beyond that card's
were lost.

A nested field now goes by position (`details.#2.rate`, the Bag `#n`
syntax) and by that path alone; the copy takes the fields of every
copied row, and the paste resolves each position to the target's nested
row or a new one, read by the same field of another row.

The selection bar also reads whether its rows can be deleted as its menu
opens: unlocking the form with rows selected left Delete greyed out.

feat(grouplet_grid): defaultRow ==expressions and additem_focus

A `defaultRow` value written `==expression` is worked out each time a
row is made (add, blank row, entry row, paste), with `this` the grid's
node and `rows` (the grid's Bag) and `grid` as arguments:
`code='==nextCode(rows)'` proposes the next code. A fresh row left empty
is measured on the defaults it was given, since the expression worked
out again may differ.

`additem_focus='<field>'` puts the caret on the editor bound to that
field of a row added with +, instead of the first one. In lazy tabs the
focus waits for the body to be mounted, and reads the tile's DOM at that
time: the mount renders the wrapper anew, so a new tab got no focus.

feat(doc): one documentation address for grouplets, fields and handbook pages

sys/ep_doc serves a doc address `<kind>:<target>:<name>` to a registered
calling page of a logged, non-guest user:
- grouplet:<pkg.table|pkg>:<resource> - the card `doc` of the resource
  (inline or file:), optionally restricted by the card's `doc_tags`
- help:<pkg.table>[/<resourceClass>]:<helpcode> - the developer-edited help
- docu:[<table>]:<hierarchical name> - a handbook page, as a page of its own

With _fragment the popup gets {title, html} (a grouplet doc is its
template, filled in the browser on the card's data, so the row values
never leave the client) or {title, page}; otherwise the full page.

- EndpointPermission (gnrcomponents/externalcall) holds the calling-page
  check that ep_table had inline; its tag check now calls
  checkResourcePermission (getResourcePermission does not exist)
- a card or grid whose resource declares a doc carries its address
  instead of the doc text; the doc is fetched once per page as it opens
- genro.dlg.docPopup / docSource / openDoc / docUrl: one popup for the
  page, used by the card ⓘ and by the helperbutton, which now shows the
  help to users (the developer's in-place editing is unchanged)
- docu.documentation.documentRst shared by docu/index/rst and ep_doc
- saveHelperValue creates the helper folder of a table that has none

fix(clipboard,grouplet): a refused copy is reported; row tools sit side by side (#1730)

genro.textToClipboard told nothing when the browser refused the write, and
raised where navigator.clipboard is missing (plain http off localhost). It
now falls back to a hidden textarea outside secure contexts, shows an error
message when the copy fails, runs the caller's message only on success and
resolves to whether the text was copied. The core callers that wrote to
navigator.clipboard directly (dom copyInClipboard, domsource, toast, form
and grid copy) go through it.

groupletGrid struct rows with delitem and editmenu drew the trash over the
kebab. The row tools now take slots side by side from the right edge, and
the row, header and footer reserve their room (grouplet_grid--tools-N).
New copyitem=True (copyitem_kwargs) shows Copy as a button out of the
kebab, as delitem does for Delete; editmenu=True then leaves Copy out.

feat(grouplet): groupletCard, a grouplet with its chrome band, alone or in a groupletGrid

The card (grouplet_card.js, gnr.GroupletCard)
- One band along the top, left or right side: tree chevron (rotates on
  open/fold), title, doc icon, then kebab and checkbox; the band is the
  drag source. Folded, a card is its band. Larger on touch screens.
- A field in error inside the card, open or folded, tints the band a very
  light red that never reads as a selection.
- The doc icon opens one popup for the page with a template rendered on
  the card data: inline, or a file next to the resource with its images.

pane.groupletCard(...)
- A titled group that can take a roundedGroup's place in a form: without
  resource or handler it returns its body, filled in place.
- Its profile (chromeSide, collapsible, title/titleTemplate/titleField,
  emptyTitle, tools, doc, doc_kw, delitem, editmenu) is the resource's
  `card` in its __info__, then what the caller gives. collapsible is False
  by default; collapsed and checkbox can live at paths of the page.
- delitem is True, False or '^path' / '=path' / '==expr' read as the menu
  opens; on a card alone the entry clears the card's own fields.
- useForm=True edits the grouplet in a GroupletForm of its own, written
  back on save and reloaded with the form around the card.

groupletGrid
- With chromeSide each card is a gnr.GroupletCard; collapsedTemplate (or
  titleTemplate) is the band title, refreshed while the card is open.
- The card profile comes from the resource (per row with resourceField)
  and card_* kwargs; delitem can be dynamic, read on the row.
- Without chromeSide the corner chrome is unchanged, same DOM.
- Template fields a row lacks render blank instead of 'undefined'.
- The drag image of a card is drawn in a copy of its grid, above the
  page, at the card's width.

Test page gnrwdg/test_grouplet_card (cases 0-9), test resource
card_profile; JS tests grouplet_card.test.js and grid tests; Python tests
grouplet_card_test.py.

feat(grouplet_grid): drag opens a slot where the rows will land

- Dragged rows lift out of the grid and leave a slot in their place; the
  slot follows the pointer, before or after the nearest row (rows by
  height, cards side by side by width), and the rows around it slide
  aside (FLIP). The drop lands in the slot: '<key' or '>key'.
- Dropped at home nothing moves; over no grid the slot goes back home; a
  drag that ends nowhere, or Esc, puts the rows back.
- One slot for the page: it moves across grids sharing a dragCode and
  opens at the level that takes the drag in nested grids; over the add
  button or the blank row it opens at the tail.
- Leaving a grid is told by a document dragover, not by dragleave, whose
  relatedTarget is often null; the slot holds still while rows slide.
- While the slot is open the row and the grid under the pointer are not
  tinted; a refused drop still is. Tabs keep the insert-after drop.
- prefers-reduced-motion keeps the slot without the animations.

Tests: slot side and nearest row, the whole drag in one grid, home, leave
and lost drag; the DnD test surfaces get a minimal DOM.

* fix(gnrjs): take the remote content lock before anything that can re-enter

updateRemoteContent set _remotebuilding only right before the rpc. On the
way there, the first _T('Loading content') of a page is a sync
getRemoteTranslation call, and in dojo 1.1 every XHR runs _watchInFlight,
which delivers any async response already in: a form load delivered there
changes a remote attribute, updateRemoteContent runs again, finds no lock
and sends its own fetch, then the outer call sends the one it was preparing
with the old attributes. Two fetches race on the same node and the last to
land is mounted: a groupletWizard showed a step's content under another
step in the stepper.

_releaseRemoteUpdate on every exit (cached attributes, false _if, landing),
which also runs the pending re-fetch.

* fix(core): publish gnrImport path modules first-wins under concurrency

gnrImport stored the module in sys.modules only after exec, so two
threads racing on the same not-yet-cached file could both execute it
and publish two distinct module objects (last-wins): callers ended up
holding different class objects for the same implementation, breaking
identity-based checks such as isinstance.

Publish with sys.modules.setdefault so all racing callers converge on
the first published module instance, except when the caller passes
avoid_module_cache=True: an explicit fresh re-import (dev-mode page
reload, grouplet/settings resources) must win over and replace the
cached module.

A full per-key import lock was deliberately avoided: holding a global
lock across exec_module can deadlock against the interpreter per-module
import locks.

* fix(services): resolve a service implementation explicitly, never by substitution

An implementation that could not be resolved was silently replaced by
baseImplementation, which is not a chosen default but the first module the
filesystem happened to return and that imported successfully. A service type
configured with an implementation that fails to import, or whose name carries
a typo, received a different class while service_implementation kept recording
the name that was asked for.

Resolution now has three branches:

- an implementation requested by name resolves or raises: it is never
  substituted;
- with no name and a single implementation, that one is used;
- with no name and several, the service type must declare
  defaultImplementation; otherwise it raises.

The failure reason is kept per implementation while the registry is built and
carried into the exception, so diagnosing an unresolved implementation no
longer requires grepping the site log for an earlier line.

_buildImplementations now catches any exception instead of ImportError alone:
a module raising something else at import time used to escape and leave the
whole service type's registry unusable, its healthy siblings included.

StorageServiceType.getServiceFactory is removed: it existed to opt storage out
of the fallback, which is now the general rule.

Behaviour changes for existing configurations: a service naming an
implementation that does not resolve, and a service on a type with several
implementations naming none, both now raise at first use instead of quietly
receiving another implementation.

* fix(services): an unresolved implementation fails on use, not at registration

Refusing to substitute another implementation is the point of this branch, but
raising while the service is being registered makes an accessory service take
down the whole site: an instance whose sms service still names an
implementation it no longer carries stopped rendering pages, on a
configuration that had been merely wrong until then.

Registration now logs the error and registers GnrUnresolvedService in place of
the service. Every attribute access and every call on it raises the same error,
naming the implementation and the reason, so the misconfiguration surfaces
where the service is used and nothing silently takes its place. A site that
never touches the service starts as before.

The placeholder answers dunder lookups with AttributeError, so hasattr, copy
and pickle keep behaving; it reports the implementation that was asked for,
never a substitute; and it carries _config_from_db, so a configuration fixed in
sys.service is picked up on the next read exactly as a working one is.

to the traceback that instance already carries, so the chain grew on every use

used 200 times from a frame holding a 256 KB local: 52.5 MB retained after a
collection, against nothing when the exception is rebuilt.

while a service is misconfigured is a site that keeps touching it, from the
mail proxy, the websocket handler, the translation service and the login
resource. The leak was fed by the design rather than by an edge case, and it
presents as unexplained worker growth with no log line naming services.

Each use now raises a new GnrException carrying the same text, chained to the
recorded reason, and the registration error keeps its own traceback empty.
The docstring also stops promising more than it delivers: only dunder lookups
answer AttributeError, so hasattr() on this object raises like the call it
precedes and is not a safe probe.

* fix(services): make implementations registry thread-safe and fail loudly

* fix(core): publish gnrImport path modules first-wins under concurrency

gnrImport stored the module in sys.modules only after exec, so two
threads racing on the same not-yet-cached file could both execute it
and publish two distinct module objects (last-wins): callers ended up
holding different class objects for the same implementation, breaking
identity-based checks such as isinstance.

Publish with sys.modules.setdefault so all racing callers converge on
the first published module instance, except when the caller passes
avoid_module_cache=True: an explicit fresh re-import (dev-mode page
reload, grouplet/settings resources) must win over and replace the
cached module.

lock across exec_module can deadlock against the interpreter per-module
import locks.

fix: make the relative storage service usable (#1182)

* fix: make the relative storage service usable

The relative storage implementation never worked: it tried to strip the
StorageService methods from a fresh instance with delattr and then to morph the
instance into the parent service class, so creating one always failed with
"AttributeError: 'Service' object has no attribute '_call'".

A relative service is now built as a subclass of the parent service class: it
reuses the parent implementation and every parameter it is configured with
(base path, bucket, credentials...) and only overrides the base path, adding
the configured relative path. This is the point of the implementation: publish
a subfolder of an existing storage as a service of its own without repeating
any parameter. A relative service can also be the parent of another one.

A service record is created before its parameters are filled in, so a relative
service with no usable parent is an ordinary state and not an error: it now
behaves as an empty storage instead of raising, otherwise the storage tree of
the very form where the parent gets chosen fails on the service it configures.
Writing on it is still refused: nothing can be written where there is no path.

The parameters form now lets any configured storage service be chosen as
parent (built-in and siteconfig ones included), instead of the sole services
registered in sys.service.

The service parameters pane is rebuilt on every record load, and the form kept
the validations of the widgets destroyed by the rebuild: on a new record the
status stayed invalid whatever was chosen. It now forgets them, the same way
the bagField and grouplet dynamic contents already do.

Fixes #834

* fix: refuse a relative storage whose parent cannot be resolved

Both cases were reachable from the parameters form, which offers every storage
service as a parent, relative ones included.

A parent that is not configured any more was resolved through the legacy
fallback of the storage handler, which serves an unknown storage name as a new
folder of the site static dir: a relative service silently re-rooted there,
writing documents in a freshly created directory somewhere else with no error
and no log. The parent is now looked up in the stored parameters first, and a
missing one leaves the service unconfigured.

A loop in the configuration (a service pointing at itself, or two pointing at
each other) ended in RecursionError: the instance of a service is cached only
once it is built, so resolving the parent recursed until the stack ended. The
chain of relative parents is now walked on the stored parameters before the
parent gets built.

For the same reason a parent with no base path at all is refused too: a local
service with no base path resolves to None, and the relative path would end up
resolved from the current working directory of the process. This also stops the
chain on a relative parent that is unconfigured itself.

Deleting on an unconfigured service now fails like the other write operations,
instead of being a silent no-op, and renameNode and duplicateNode raise the
message of the class instead of AttributeError.

* fix(core): publish gnrImport path modules first-wins under concurrency

gnrImport stored the module in sys.modules only after exec, so two
threads racing on the same not-yet-cached file could both execute it
and publish two distinct module objects (last-wins): callers ended up
holding different class objects for the same implementation, breaking
identity-based checks such as isinstance.

Publish with sys.modules.setdefault so all racing callers converge on
the first published module instance, except when the caller passes
avoid_module_cache=True: an explicit fresh re-import (dev-mode page
reload, grouplet/settings resources) must win over and replace the
cached module.

A full per-key import lock was deliberately avoided: holding a global
lock across exec_module can deadlock against the interpreter per-module
import locks.

feat(groupletGrid): new widget for Bag-driven repeatable mini-forms

Introduce `groupletGrid`, a genropy widget that renders a Bag as N
tiles where each tile is the same reusable "grouplet" template (a
mini-form). One RPC for the row template, then zero RPC for the
rest — every add/remove/edit/save flows through Bag triggers.

The widget covers a spectrum of use cases that don't fit a flat
gnr.Grid: invoice line editors, kanban boards, framed card galleries,
spreadsheet-style data entry, multi-pane tab editors, and recursive
master-detail forms. A demo gallery (`11_grouplet_grid.py`) walks
through twelve scenarios.

## Architecture

* **Python** (`grouplet.py`): `gr_groupletGrid(storepath, resource|
  handler|struct, layout=, dragCode=, ...)` emits a CSS-grid
  container with autoslots (top/bottom/left/right), a sibling
  BagStore for change/lock/delete integration, and a `_onBuilt`
  dataController that boots the JS controller. Templates are
  resolved server-side via `gr_getGroupletGridTemplate`.

* **JS** (`grouplet_grid.js`): four `gnr.*` classes —
  - `GroupletGridStructAdapter`: maps a Grid-style `struct` (cells +
    dtype/edit/totalize/formula) to a spreadsheet-like tile.
  - `GroupletGridDnD`: DOM-pure HTML5 drag-and-drop dispatcher
    shared by tile (cards/struct) and chip (tabs/vtabs). Same
    payload (`gg_tile_<dragCode>`), same move dispatch.
  - `GroupletGridController`: orchestrates lifecycle, action bus
    (`groupletGrid_<nodeId>_action`), layout switching, template
    loading (with `resourceField=` multi-template mode), struct
    chrome alignment, and the `GridChangeManager` bridge for
    formulas / totalizers / filtered totals.
  - `GroupletGridTile`: per-pkey view (chrome `×`/kebab/drag handle
    + body grafted from a deep-copied template with namespaced
    nodeIds).
  - `GroupletDataStore`: thin view over the sibling BagStore;
    forwards getData / addRow / removeRow / moveRow / updateRow /
    deleteRowAsk / hasChanges / hasErrors / setLocked / sum to the
    standard `gnr.stores.ValuesBagRows` API.

* **CSS** (`grouplet.css`): theme tokens, layout primitives for the
  cards / tabs / vtabs / struct modes, DnD state classes aligned
  with framework conventions (`draggedItem`, `canBeDropped`,
  `cannotBeDropped`, `body.drag_started`).

## Design decisions

* **Sibling BagStore is mandatory** (default `storeType='ValuesBagRows'`).
  Wires `attr.store=<bagStore nodeId>` on the container; the
  dataStore looks it up via `genro.nodeById`. Mandatory because
  every meaningful integration (changeManager, deleteAsk, future
  phantomForm and filter-aware totals) hangs off the store.

* **`_namespaceFrameworkNodeIds` rewrites every `grpgrid_*` string
  attr**, not just `nodeId`. Required so cross-references inside
  cloned templates (`attr.store`, `dragCode`, etc.) stay consistent
  per row. Side effect: `dragCode=None` (default-isolated) is now
  genuinely per-instance; cross-grid sharing requires an explicit
  string dragCode.

* **DOM-pure DnD on both tile and chip**, no framework
  `dropTarget`/`onDrag_*` kwargs. Same pattern as the existing chip
  path, decoupled from `getInheritedAttributes` / pointer-events
  cascades that broke nested grids.

* **Move dispatch splices `bag._nodes` in place** (no `popNode +
  setItem(_position)`). Nested widgets anchored at the moved row's
  datapath would otherwise see "unresolved relativepath".

* **Construct-time controller work deferred to
  `genro.src.onBuiltCall`**. Same pattern as gnr.Grid
  (genro_grid.js:704): cloned templates finish building their inner
  BagStore after the controller's own `_onBuilt` fires.

up at first use. The container exposes `attr.store=<bagStore nodeId>`;
the dataStore resolves it lazily and forwards getData / sum /

  in cloned templates, not just `attr.nodeId`. The container's

fix(groupletGrid): full-tile drop area + self-drop feedback

Two related bugs surfaced when the declarative DnD pattern landed:

1. The drop area felt narrow: hovering over an inner widget (input,
   button) of the tile failed to activate the drop highlight. The user
   had to find a "gap" between widgets to land on the wrapper.
2. Dragging a tile back onto itself still highlighted as a valid drop
   instead of showing the `cannotBeDropped` (forbidden) outline.

Root cause #1: the framework's getEventInfo resolves the innermost
sourceNode under the cursor. Inner widgets are themselves sourceNodes
without `dropTarget` declared, so the drop is rejected for the wrong
sourceNode. Fix: while `body.drag_started` is set (by the framework
during any drag), suppress pointer-events on all direct children of
`.grouplet_grid_row`, except the drag handle itself which stays
grabbable for dragend bubbling. The tile rectangle becomes the single
contiguous drop target.

Root cause #2: the framework computes `info.selfdrop` by comparing
`info.nodeId` (drop target sourceNode nodeId) with
`info.dragSourceInfo.nodeId` (drag source sourceNode nodeId). Our drag
source is the `⠿` handle sub-sourceNode (auto-generated nodeId),
while the drop target is the tile sourceNode (our `tileNodeId`).
They never match, so `info.selfdrop` was always false. Fix: in the
handle's `onDrag_<type>` callback, override `dragInfo.nodeId =
tile.tileNodeId` BEFORE the framework calls setDragSourceInfo. Now the
identity recorded in the dragsourceinfo payload is the tile's, and
`info.selfdrop` resolves correctly when the user drops on the source
tile. The new `dropTargetCb` on the tile reads `dropInfo.selfdrop` and
returns false → framework paints `cannotBeDropped`.

While here, align CSS class names with the framework convention so the
framework's automatic class toggling (genro_dom.js:1086-1095) drives
our styling directly:
  .gg-drop-target          → .canBeDropped
  .gg-drop-target-invalid  → .cannotBeDropped
  .gg-dragging             → .draggedItem (framework's default dragClass)
  .gg-drag-active (on container) → body.drag_started (framework scope)

The same renames are applied to the legacy chip/container DnD (still
wired manually as Option B) so the visual feedback stays uniform during
the transition.

`gg-just-dropped` is kept (it's our own post-drop flash, not framework
managed).

refactor(groupletGrid): store-driven dispatch via gnr_storepath

Move the controller to a single-source-of-truth architecture: the Bag at
`storepath` is the only state, and every mutation flows through one
dispatch entry point. The previous custom `_trigger_data` + `getTriggerReason`
pipeline (which mixed Bag mutation and DOM build in the same scope) is
replaced by the canonical genropy `mixin_setStorepath` pattern:

  python:  node.externalWidget = node.gridController
           node.registerDynAttr('storepath')
           node._setDynAttributes()

  js:      gnr_storepath(value, kw, trigger_reason)

The framework dispatches via gnrdomsource.js:1357-1363
(doUpdateAttrBuiltObj → externalWidget['gnr_'+attr]). Pattern reference:
FullCalendar in genro_extra.js:124-129 + 145.

Inside `gnr_storepath` the level of the mutation is discriminated via
`kw.node.parentshipLevel(storeNode)`, same as gnrgrid.mixin_setStorepath
(genro_grid.js:2953):

  parent_lv === 0 → whole-store replacement (newDataStore equivalent)
                    → _renderFromStore() rebuilds from scratch
  parent_lv === 1 → row added/removed at the rows-Bag root
                    → _addRow(rowKey) or _removeRow(rowKey)
  parent_lv  > 1  → mutation INSIDE a row (a field, a sub-bag)
                    → no-op: the widget bound to that path updates itself

Consequences:

* `_doAddRow` / `_doDeleteRow` / `_doMoveRow` / `_doMoveRowSameInstance`
  / `_doMoveRowFrom` now only mutate the Bag — they no longer touch the
  DOM directly. Drop happens via `popNode + setItem({_position})` on a
  single Bag (no more parallel body-source Bag bookkeeping).

* `_addRow` derives the wrapper insertion position by walking the rows
  Bag once: insert before the next sibling that is already in the DOM,
  or append. Works uniformly for action handlers, DnD, and external
  setItem from outside the controller.

* `_pendingFlash` map carries the "just-dropped" visual marker across
  the dispatch boundary: `_doMoveRow*` set the flag before the Bag
  mutation, `_addRow` consumes it when the trigger-driven re-render
  lands. Bespoke pattern — no canonical genropy equivalent.

* External Bag mutations (serverCall, console, page-level dataController)
  now propagate to the grid for free, since they trigger the same
  dispatch chain. Test_1 has been reshaped to exercise this: starts
  empty + a `Load sample` button swaps the whole rows Bag in via
  dataFormula — exercises the parent_lv === 0 branch (newDataStore).

* `storepath` is the path as declared by the author (no `^`/`==` magic
  yet); the controller resolves it once in the constructor via
  `sourceNode.absDatapath(sourceNode.attr.storepath)`. The body div
  carries `datapath=storepath` so each row wrapper, created with
  `datapath='.<rowKey>'`, resolves its inline widgets' `^.field`
  references against the matching node in the rows Bag.

* `storebag()` helper does a fresh `genro.getData(this.storepath)` on
  every call, mirroring `gnrgrid.mixin_storebag` (genro_grid.js:3230-3236).

Dead code removed: `_registerTriggers`, `_onDataChange`,
`_handleChildChange`, `getTriggerReason`-based filtering, `_synthetic`
init events, the stale `bodyNode.unregisterSubscription` in `destroy`,
and a couple of Italian narrative comments left over from the previous

The Python widget body no longer derives its `datapath` from `storepath`

- Two-bag pattern: `addRowAction` and `deleteRowAction` mutate both
  the data Bag (user values) and the source Bag (DOM tree) explicitly.
  The `_trigger_data` subscription on the bodyNode does not fire from
  data Bag mutations — they're separate dispatchers — so the dual
  mutation is required.
- Atomic widget construction: `_addRow` uses
  `wrapperNode.freeze()` -> `_graftNode` recursive -> `wrapperNode.unfreeze()`
  so widgets are built with their labels in one rebuild pass.
  `_fullSync` (init batch) freezes/unfreezes the whole bodyNode for
  N rows in a single pass.
- Server-side `body_datapath`: the `<div class="grouplet_grid_body">`
  has its `datapath` set at template emission time (cannot be patched
  at runtime — the binding is consumed during DOM construction).
